title: To it or with it: -kan and -i
goal: Choose between the two suffixes that decide what a verb's object is: *-kan* makes the thing that moves the object, *-i* makes the place or the person on the receiving end the object. Along the way, meet the everyday *-i* verbs of going to people and places: *mendekati, menemui, mengunjungi*.
bekal: say the same thing two ways: *mengirimkan foto ke Rina* and *mengirimi Rina foto*
water, plant and pour with the right suffix: *menyirami tanaman*, *menyiramkan air*, *menanami pot*
visit, meet and approach people politely: *mengunjungi sekolah*, *menemui Bapak*, *mendekati siswa*

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Halaman yang masih kosong
dialogs.intro: Sunday morning. Bu Endang leans over the low wall between the two houses and looks at Sarah's bare front yard with open disappointment.

lines.speaker: Endang:
lines.text: Mbak Sarah, halamannya kok masih kosong? Sayang, lho.
lines.id: Mbak Sarah, how come your yard is still empty? It's such a waste.
lines.literal: Miss Sarah, yard-the [kok] still empty? pity, [lho].

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Iya, Bu. Saya belum sempat menanam apa-apa.
lines.id: I know. I haven't got round to planting anything.
lines.literal: yes, Mrs. I not-yet have-time plant anything.

lines.speaker: Endang:
lines.text: Ini saya bawakan bibit cabai sama kemangi. Pot-pot kosong itu kita tanami saja, ya.
lines.id: Here, I've brought you some chilli and basil seedlings. Let's plant up those empty pots.
lines.literal: this I bring-for seedling chilli with basil. pot-pot empty that we plant-in just, yes.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Wah, matur nuwun, Bu. Potnya harus saya isi tanah dulu?
lines.id: Oh, thank you so much. Do I need to fill the pots with soil first?
lines.literal: wow, thank you, Mrs. pot-the must I fill soil first?

lines.speaker: Endang:
lines.text: Iya, diisi setengah dulu. Terus bibitnya ditanam di tengah.
lines.id: Yes, fill them halfway first. Then the seedlings go in the middle.
lines.literal: yes, is-filled half first. then seedling-the is-planted at middle.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Setelah itu langsung disirami?
lines.id: And then we water them straight away?
lines.literal: after that straight-away is-watered?

lines.speaker: Endang:
lines.text: Disirami sedikit saja. Jangan siramkan air terlalu banyak, nanti akarnya busuk.
lines.id: Just a little. Don't pour too much water on them, or the roots will rot.
lines.literal: is-watered a-little just. don't pour-on water too much, later root-the rotten.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Baik. Jadi setiap pagi saya sirami, Bu?
lines.id: Right. So I water them every morning?
lines.literal: good. so every morning I water, Mrs?

lines.speaker: Endang:
lines.text: Pagi sama sore, kalau nggak hujan. Kalau Mbak ke Jakarta, nanti saya yang menyirami.
lines.id: Morning and evening, if it hasn't rained. When you go to Jakarta, I'll do the watering.
lines.literal: morning with afternoon, if not rain. if Miss to Jakarta, later I the-one-who water.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Terima kasih, Bu. Nanti fotonya saya kirimkan ke Rina. Dia pasti iri.
lines.id: Thank you. I'll send a photo to Rina. She'll be green with envy.
lines.literal: thank you, Mrs. later photo-the I send to Rina. she surely envious.

lines.speaker: Endang:
lines.text: Kalau sudah panen, kirimi dia cabainya sekalian!
lines.id: Once you've harvested, send her some of the chillies while you're at it!
lines.literal: if already harvest, send-to her chilli-the at-the-same-time!

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Ha-ha, boleh. Dimas boleh ikut merawat, Bu?
lines.id: Ha, why not. Can Dimas help look after them?
lines.literal: ha-ha, may. Dimas may join tend, Mrs?

lines.speaker: Endang:
lines.text: Harus! Biar dari kecil sudah ditanamkan rasa sayang sama tanaman.
lines.id: He has to! That way a love of plants is instilled in him from an early age.
lines.literal: must! so-that from small already is-planted-in feeling love with plant.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Setuju. Asal bolanya jangan mendekati pot cabai, ya.
lines.id: Agreed. As long as his football stays away from the chilli pots.
lines.literal: agree. as-long-as ball-his don't approach pot chilli, yes.

notes: **Kok masih kosong? Sayang, lho.** *Kok* marks surprise: “how come…?”. *Sayang* here is not “darling” but “what a pity” — the same word, used about wasted chances. *Lho* adds a gentle nudge of emphasis, and in Yogyakarta you will hear it in almost every other sentence.

**Pot-pot itu kita tanami.** The object-focus shape from Unit 4: the thing first, then the doer, then the bare verb with no *me-*. *Tanami* has *-i*, so its object is the pot, the place being planted. The ordinary active would be *Kita menanami pot-pot itu*.

**Matur nuwun** is Javanese for “thank you”, and Sarah is showing off a little. Everyone in Yogya understands it, older people love hearing it, and *terima kasih* remains the Indonesian you can use anywhere in the country.

**Disirami, siramkan.** The root *siram* is “to pour water”. *Menyirami tanaman* is to water the plants: the plants receive the water, so *-i*. *Menyiramkan air* is to pour the water: the water moves, so *-kan*. Bu Endang uses both in one breath, which is exactly how you will hear them.

**Kirimi dia cabainya!** Commands drop the *me-* but keep the suffix: *Kirimi!* (send to someone), *Kirimkan!* (send something), *Siramkan!*, *Tanami!*. And look at the order: with *-i* the person, *dia*, comes straight after the verb, and the chillies come second.

**Menanamkan** literally means “to plant something into”, but in real life it is used almost only for values and habits: *menanamkan disiplin*, *menanamkan rasa sayang*, to instil. For actual seedlings Indonesians say *menanam cabai* or *menanami pot*.

grammars.title: -kan moves the thing, -i targets the place or the person
body: Many roots take both suffixes. The action is the same; what changes is which word becomes the object. Ask yourself: is the object the thing that travels, or the place or person where it lands?

head: Root
-kan: the thing is the object
-i: the place or person is the object

after: With *-kan* the receiver needs a preposition: *ke* for places and people in everyday speech, *kepada* for people in careful Indonesian. With *-i* the receiver sits straight after the verb with no preposition at all.
⚠️ Do not mix the two patterns. *Saya mengirimi foto ke Rina* is a classic learner sentence and sounds broken to Indonesians. Either *mengirimkan foto ke Rina* or *mengirimi Rina foto*.
💬 In speech the *-kan* is often dropped altogether: *Nanti saya kirim ke Rina.* It is the *-i* that people keep, because without it the meaning changes.

grammars.title: The suffix survives every shape
body: Whatever you do to the front of the verb, the suffix at the back stays put. Here is *sirami* and *siramkan* in the four shapes you now know.
after: The last row is worth copying. A polite request in Indonesian is very often a passive: *Tolong disirami* — literally “please, let it be watered”. It sounds softer than *Tolong sirami*, because it doesn't point at the listener.
💬 Bu Endang's other spoken words: *sama* for *dan* (and), *terus* for *lalu* (then), *biar* for *supaya* (so that). All three are normal in relaxed speech everywhere; write the standard ones.

dialogs.title: Second dialogue — Kunjungan ke sekolah mitra
dialogs.intro: Tuesday. Sarah visits a state senior high school in Bantul, one of the partner schools for the office's new English programme. The head teacher, Pak Yusuf, meets her at the gate.

lines.speaker: Yusuf:
lines.text: Selamat pagi, Mbak Sarah. Terima kasih sudah mengunjungi sekolah kami.
lines.id: Good morning, Ms Sarah. Thank you for visiting our school.
lines.literal: safe morning, Miss Sarah. thank you already visit school we.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Sama-sama, Pak. Saya senang sekali bisa menemui Bapak langsung.
lines.id: My pleasure. I'm very glad to be able to see you in person.
lines.literal: same-same, Sir. I happy very can go-and-see you directly.

lines.speaker: Yusuf:
lines.text: Surat dari kantor Mbak sudah kami terima minggu lalu.
lines.id: We received the letter from your office last week.
lines.literal: letter from office Miss already we receive week past.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Syukurlah. Kami juga sudah menerima jadwal kegiatan yang Bapak kirimkan.
lines.id: I'm glad. And we've received the schedule of activities you sent.
lines.literal: thank-God. we also already receive schedule activity that you send.

lines.speaker: Yusuf:
lines.text: Nanti Mbak bisa menemui para siswa kelas sebelas di aula.
lines.id: In a moment you can meet the Year 11 students in the hall.
lines.literal: later Miss can go-and-see [plural] student class eleven at hall.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Baik. Mereka sudah tahu tentang program ini?
lines.id: Good. Do they already know about the programme?
lines.literal: good. they already know about programme this?

lines.speaker: Yusuf:
lines.text: Sudah. Tapi mereka agak malu kalau didekati orang asing.
lines.id: Yes. But they're a bit shy when a foreigner comes up to them.
lines.literal: already. but they rather shy if is-approached person foreign.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Tidak apa-apa, Pak. Saya akan mendekati mereka pelan-pelan.
lines.id: That's all right. I'll approach them gently.
lines.literal: not what-what, Sir. I will approach them slow-slow.

lines.speaker: Yusuf:
lines.text: Bagus. Kalau ada pertanyaan, silakan hubungi Bu Rahma, wali kelasnya.
lines.id: Good. If you have any questions, please contact Bu Rahma, their form teacher.
lines.literal: good. if exist question, please contact Mrs Rahma, guardian class-their.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Nomor Bu Rahma boleh Bapak kirimkan ke saya?
lines.id: Could you send me Bu Rahma's number?
lines.literal: number Mrs Rahma may you send to me?

lines.speaker: Yusuf:
lines.text: Tentu. Mari, saya antarkan ke aula.
lines.id: Of course. This way, I'll take you to the hall.
lines.literal: certainly. let-us, I take to hall.

notes: **Mengunjungi sekolah kami.** *Mengunjungi* is “to visit” and it takes its object directly. ⚠️ *mengunjungi ke sekolah* is a very common mistake: the *-i* already contains the “to”. If you want *ke*, use the plain verb *berkunjung ke sekolah*.

**Menemui vs bertemu.** *Bertemu dengan Pak Yusuf* just means the two of you meet. *Menemui Pak Yusuf* means you go and see him on purpose, usually for business. Sarah's choice is slightly formal and exactly right for a head teacher.

**Sudah kami terima.** Object-focus again, with *kami*. In an official conversation Pak Yusuf speaks for the whole school, so *kami* (we, not including you) is the natural pronoun, and the letter comes first because it is the topic.

**Para siswa.** *Para* marks a group of people and makes the noun plural without doubling it: *para siswa, para guru, para peserta*. It is a written, slightly formal word, and ⚠️ never *para siswa-siswa*.
**Didekati orang asing** — the passive of *mendekati*, with the doer placed right after the verb and no *oleh*. This is the normal way to say who does it in a *di-* sentence when the doer is short.

**Mari, saya antarkan.** *Mari* is the polite form of *ayo* and here means “this way, please”. *Mengantarkan* (spoken *nganterin* in Jakarta, *nganter* in Yogya) is to take or accompany someone somewhere, and Indonesians do it for guests as a matter of course.

grammars.title: -i verbs of going to someone or somewhere
body: A group of very common verbs use *-i* to mean “to go to, to come near, to be at” something. Their object is the place or the person, with no preposition.

head: Plain verb + preposition
-i verb + object
English
rows: to go and see Pak Yusuf
to come to the house (on purpose)

after: The left-hand column is ordinary and friendly; the right-hand column is a little more formal and is what you will read in letters, news and school notices. Both are correct, but never combine them: not *menghadiri di rapat*, not *memasuki ke ruangan*.

sections.title: Adjectives that become verbs with -kan or -i

blocks.text: The same logic works on adjectives. With *-kan* you make something have that quality, or move it that way; with *-i* you do something to a person or place from that position. Some pairs drift quite far apart in meaning, so learn them as pairs.

head: Root
-kan
English
-i
English
rows: to dirty, make a mess of

blocks.text: *Memanasi motor* — letting the motorbike engine run for a minute before you ride off — is a morning ritual on every street in Yogya. *Menerangkan* for “to explain” comes from the idea of making something bright and clear; its everyday synonym is *menjelaskan*, built the same way from *jelas*.

sections.title: Everyday -i verbs you will hear this week

blocks.text: Some *-i* verbs have no *-kan* partner in daily use. Their object is simply the person or thing that receives the feeling or the action. Learn them whole.
